title: 建议添加整理导出聊天记录的功能，输出报告
body:
很多时候，我们需要把chatgpt的反馈转发给其它人、或者自己的其它设备，或用来存储备份。
目前我能想到的数据保存、传递方式无非就是
1、复制文本或截图后发送。
2、导出本地聊天数据。
3、利用一些第三方的浏览器插件比如印象笔记的插件。
这些方式都可以解决一部分需求，但都不能充分发挥第三方软件的优势：那就是对内容的强大编辑整理能力，加上GPT自己还能参与编辑，若能有这么一个功能：
1、由用户选择需要输出的聊天记录，然后让GPT整理出一份摘要，摘要也允许用户编辑。
2、提供可定制的输出模板，由软件输出为完整的报告，报告结构采用“摘要+正文（带目录）”的方式。
3、模板应有一定的基本规则，能够让查看的人一眼认出是ChatGPT生成。
4、模板应该能识别针对选定的内容由chatgpt多次生成几个备选答案，在正文中只显示一份用户选定的答案，但模板能存储所有chatgpt输出答案，提供某种方式让用户查看，这会使报告的意义更大。

这个功能会使得与ChatGPT的交互变成了更正式的“创作”，最终能以完整的报告文章的方式得到一个相对严谨的结果，可以方便的与其它用户、朋友同事进行交流。

这种报告存储格式会是个问题，也许PDF会比较容易实现，或者用mhtml的帮助格式？

title: 关于系统人设的使用体会和建议
body:
翻阅了一下源码，注意到当前调用api时总是会保留当前 chat session 的第一条 prompt，结合 clean 功能仅清除 system role 之外的消息，我猜想这里的设计初衷是希望引导用户把第一条 prompt 优先作为 system role 来使用的，这样能达到最佳的指导效果。

这几天在实际使用时，我会对不同的问答场景开不同的 chat session，这里会首先预设它的身份。目前的交互是：
先发一条 prompt 预设其身份，一些指导性的 context 以及输入输出的用例指导。等回复后，我会把第一条消息 edit 一下，把 role 改成 system，然后 clean 掉 bot 无意义的答复，再开始提出实际的问题。接下来再把交互中新产生的一些有用的背景知识 edit 到第一条 system 消息里。这个 session 就成了未来相同场景下的专家了。

这里想说的是，是否可以将 system role 的 prompt 单独地做成一个 chat session 的配置项，而不是默认总拼接第一条？而且在设置 system 的时候，不需要发出 api 请求？主要是这几点：
1. system role 本是可选的，尤其是一些简单提问场景下，不太能预设第一条一定是人设型的问题。
2. 当需要设定 system role 时，能更直观和方便，且不会产生多余的 api 调用
3. 这个 system role 的 prompt 可以通过置顶或者其他固定的展示方式，用于提示这个chat session的基本设定，而不用一直往上翻来确认和编辑

```
sudo dpkg -i chatbox_0.2.7_amd64.deb

使用 dpkg 安装 deb 之后点击图表无法启动应用

## 问题原因:
在终端中输入
```
> chatbox
chatbox: error while loading shared libraries: libssl.so.1.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory

发现缺少动态库

```
wget http://nz2.archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/pool/main/o/openssl/libssl1.1_1.1.1f-1ubuntu2.17_amd64.deb

Problem Description
I am using the ChatBox Git project for development, but I am unable to use it when connected to a network with a firewall or restricted internet access. This is because the ChatBox tool does not currently support HTTP or SOCKS proxies, which are necessary for accessing the internet in these types of network environments.

Proposed Solution
I would like to request that the ChatBox Git project add functionality for HTTP and SOCKS proxies. This would allow users to connect to the internet through a proxy server, bypassing the restrictions of the network they are on. This would greatly improve the accessibility and flexibility of the ChatBox tool.

Additional Context
As a developer, I often work in environments with restricted internet access, which makes it difficult for me to use the ChatBox tool. Adding support for HTTP and SOCKS proxies would make it possible for me to use the tool in these environments, increasing my productivity and making my work easier. Thank you for considering my request.

**3、拖动对话**，可拖动排列对话，使用拖动来调整对话顺序。

title: [Feature] Bulk delete and chat export / 大量刪除訊息以及聊天匯出功能
body:
**Problem Description**
Although chat tabbing is already quite useful, there may be cases where you need to remove specific requests and responses in a chat. It would be great to have a "bulk delete" feature for this purpose. Also, it would be very helpful to have the ability to export the chat as a JSON or TXT file if possible.

**Proposed Solution**
After clicking the "Bulk Delete" button (which may be located next to the "Clear" button), a checkbox will appear next to each message. Just select the checkbox next to the messages you want to delete, and then click the "Bulk Delete" button again to delete the unwanted messages. As for the "Export Chat" button, it can be set in the three-dot menu on the chat tab.

**Additional Context**
N/A

-----------------------

**问题描述**
雖然分頁已經相當實用，但在某些情況下，可能會需要某則聊天中的特定對話和回應。希望可以新增大量刪除訊息 (要求及回應) 的功能。另外，將聊天匯出為 JSON 或 TXT 檔案也會相當實用。

**解决思路**
點選「大量刪除」按鈕 (可位於「清除」按鈕旁) 後，訊息旁隨即會顯示核取方塊，只要找出要刪除的訊息並勾選旁邊的方塊，然後再次點選「大量刪除」按鈕，即可將不需要的訊息刪除。至於「匯出聊天」按鈕，則可設置於聊天分頁的三點選單中。

title: More granular control over API parameters
body:
**Problem Description**
There are not enough controls to fully fine tune the model behavior via API parameters. 

**Proposed Solution**
As of now we are only able to set "Temperature" and "Token" parameters in the app. It would be helpful if we could also set **"Top P"**, "**Frequency Penalty**", and "**Presence Penalty**" as well.

**Additional Context**
Many users of this software are power users. We need and can utilize these fine tunings appropriately. There are many use cases for changing these additional parameters beyond just Temperature controls. 

For instance, here is a scenario where "Top_p" is more beneficial than Temperature:

> Summarization of Text: When summarizing a text document, the goal is to generate a concise yet accurate summary of the original content. If we set a low top_p, the model focuses on the most probable (i.e., relevant) phrases from the text, thereby ignoring less likely tokens. This is likely to yield a more coherent and relevant summary. If, instead, we reduce the temperature, the model becomes less explorative and could overfocus on certain aspects of the document while neglecting others, leading to an unbalanced or inaccurate summary.

![2023-05-24_17h50_15](https://github.com/Bin-Huang/chatbox/assets/133587103/778536f3-f47d-4c21-b174-b55d24c61fe3)

----

As I test more models with Large Token Window, such as Claude v1.3 100k, I can feel obvious lag when the text length exceeds 30k tokens. It's basically unusable at 90k tokens. [Feature] Use Exact Token Usage In The Response Subscript

**Problem Description**
I do not know the exact number of tokens used. Instead, I have an estimated number - https://i.imgur.com/UzE1Sz2.png.
The "~" characters indicate that this is an estimate, even though there IS a way to get the exact number, not an estimation.

**Proposed Solution**
I know the OpenAI returns the exact number of API tokens used to generate an answer - https://i.imgur.com/wXAnRA9.png

You may edit the subscript in Chatbox like so:

Before
"word count: 30, token count: ~43, tokens used: ~2111, model: gpt-3.5-turbo-16k" 

After
"word count: 30, token count: [the exact number from the response], tokens used: [the exact number from the response], model: gpt-3.5-turbo-16k" 

The [] indicates a placeholder.
Notice the removed '~' characters, indicating it's no longer an estimate.

The used ~ characters are misleading, and You should remove them if the number of the tokens is exact and not an approximation.

**Additional Context**
I do not know if this was this already implemented. The ~ characters may have misled me as well.

The "~" (tilde) character often indicates an approximation. Maybe it has been misused.

Using an exact number instead of an estimate will make ChatBox look more professional and reliable.

title: [Feature] Conversation Folders for Organization and Archiving
body:
**Problem Description**
Currently all conversations in Chatbox exist in one long list which becomes difficult to manage when there are a large number of conversations. 

**Proposed Solution** 
Implement conversation archiving/grouping functionality:
- Allow users to create folders or groups to organize conversations
- Users can drag and drop conversations into these folders
- Each conversation can belong to multiple folders
- Folders should have naming, coloring, reordering capabilities
- Browsing and searching foldered conversations is easier

**Additional Context**  
Foldering can help users better organize large amounts of conversations and improve efficiency in finding and managing conversations. It also allows segmenting conversations by project, topic, client etc.
Overall, this feature can significantly optimize user workflow and experience.
For example, folders like "Client A", "Client B" can be created to separate conversations for different clients.

This is a highly demanded feature by many users. Implementing it in the next release would greatly increase user productivity and satisfaction. Please consider adding this capability.

title: [Feature] Allow Customizable Max Tokens in Context
body:
**Problem Description**
There are projects like Claude API Converter that adapt Claude's API to be compatible with OpenAI's format and allow integrating Claude with services designed for OpenAI. However, Claude supports up to 100,000 max tokens, while Chatbox has a hardcoded limit of 32,000 tokens. This makes integrating Claude inconvenient.

**Proposed Solution**  
Implement an option for users to customize Chatbox's max tokens in context setting to better support Clara and other services. 

- Add "Max Tokens in Context" configuration
- Allow values up to 100,000 to match Claude's limit
- Save user's custom max tokens value
- Use custom value when making API requests

**Benefits**
- Enables smoothly integrating Claude via existing converter projects 
- Allows fully leveraging Claude's higher context capacity
- More flexibility for power users
- Improves extensibility with other services  

**Additional Context** 
Given projects enabling Claude integration, hardcoding the max tokens in Chatbox creates an artificial barrier. Adding this customization would improve compatibility and user experience.

title: [Feature] Request for New Feature - Hotkeys for Various Actions in Application | 请求新功能 - 应用程序中各种操作的热键
body:
Problem Description
In our current application, navigating through different features and performing basic operations requires multiple taps. This can be time-consuming and may not provide the most efficient user experience, especially for power users who are familiar with the application and want to perform actions quickly.

Proposed Solution
I propose that we introduce hotkeys for various actions in our application. These hotkeys would allow users to quickly perform actions such as starting a new chat, deleting a chat, opening copilots, accessing settings options, and more. By pressing a combination of keys, users could perform these actions instantly, improving the speed and efficiency of their interaction with the application.

For example, we could assign "Ctrl + N" for starting a new chat, "Ctrl + D" for deleting a chat, "Ctrl + C" for opening copilots, and "Ctrl + S" for accessing settings options.

To implement this feature, we could utilize TypeScript libraries that are specifically designed for handling keyboard events and creating hotkeys. Libraries such as "mousetrap", "hotkeys-js", and "react-hotkeys-hook" are popular choices that offer robust functionality and are widely used in the industry.

Additional Context
Hotkeys are common in many applications and are appreciated by users for their convenience and efficiency. Implementing this feature would not only enhance our current user experience but could also attract more tech-savvy users who prefer keyboard shortcuts for their operations.

This feature could be implemented by mapping specific key combinations to their corresponding actions in the application's code using the aforementioned libraries. We would also need to ensure that these hotkeys do not conflict with existing system or application shortcuts.

Thank you for considering this feature request. I believe that the addition of hotkeys would significantly improve the user experience and efficiency of our application.

---

问题描述
在我们当前的应用程序中，浏览不同的功能并执行基本操作需要多次点击。这可能非常耗时，并且可能无法提供最有效的用户体验，特别是对于熟悉应用程序并希望快速执行操作的高级用户。

解决思路
我建议我们在应用程序中引入各种操作的热键。这些热键将允许用户快速执行诸如开始新聊天，删除聊天，打开副驾驶，访问设置选项等操作。通过按下一组键，用户可以立即执行这些操作，提高他们与应用程序交互的速度和效率。

例如，我们可以为开始新聊天分配 "Ctrl + N"，为删除聊天分配 "Ctrl + D"，为打开副驾驶分配 "Ctrl + C"，以及为访问设置选项分配 "Ctrl + S"。

为了实现这个功能，我们可以使用专门设计用于处理键盘事件和创建热键的 TypeScript 库。如 "mousetrap"，"hotkeys-js" 和 "react-hotkeys-hook" 等库是流行的选择，它们提供了强大的功能，并在业界得到了广泛的使用。

附加上下文
热键在许多应用程序中很常见，用户因其便利性和效率而赞赏它们。实施这个功能不仅会增强我们当前的用户体验，还可能吸引更多喜欢使用键盘快捷方式进行操作的技术型用户。

我们可以使用上述库将特定的键组合映射到应用程序代码中的相应操作来实现这个功能。我们还需要确保这些热键不会与现有的系统或应用程序快捷方式冲突。

感谢您考虑这个功能请求。我相信，添加热键将显著提高我们应用程序的用户体验和效率。

title: [Feature] ✨ Tab-based Layout for Multiple Drafts & 🎨 Color Coding for Speaker Identification
body:
**Problem Description**
As a user engaging in a dialogue with an LLM using ChatBox, when I prompt the model to generate different versions of responses for a single question, I find it challenging to manage these versions efficiently. Currently, all responses are displayed in a linear fashion, making the conversational context cluttered and increasing the chance of the model misinterpreting my intentions, as well as unnecessarily consuming API call quota and context window capacity.

**Proposed Solution**
1. Implement a tab-like layout, similar to browser tabs, that allows users to fold different versions of responses to the same question. For example, if I ask the AI to "write the beginning of a poem," I would want the AI to generate multiple drafts for this request. These drafts should be presented in a parallel fashion using tabs in a single row. Users can then select their preferred response version by clicking on the corresponding tab, which will incorporate only that version into the context, therefore reducing misunderstanding and saving both context space and API costs. It is important that only one draft is chosen to be displayed and considered in the subsequent context window, while all other versions are excluded from further dialogue context. This can be inspired by the layout mode used by Google Bard's web version.
2. Assign and render color-coded speech bubbles or cards for different speakers in the conversation, significantly improving the users' ability to locate information quickly. Below is an example of how this improvement could look:

```markdown
[**System**:](#ffa07a66) You are an omnipotent assistant, and I am your client. Please answer the client's questions in English.
[**User**:](#add8e670) Hello!
[**User**:](#add8e670) Can you tell me who won the last World Cup?
[**Bot**:](#dda0dd80) The last World Cup champion was Brazil.
[**User**:](#add8e670) What was the exact date of Brazil's victory?
[**Bot**:](#dda0dd80) Just a moment.
```
The tags `[**System**:](#)` and `[**User**:](#)` would be color-coded consistently throughout the conversation for easy identification.

**Additional Context**
This feature would immensely benefit users like content creators, researchers, or any user who requires precision and efficiency in conversational drafts. The tab-based response management allows users to easily compare different AI-generated drafts without the need for scrolling or searching through the context window. Additionally, the color-coding feature could allow users to visually distinguish between different dialogue participants at a glance, leading to a more intuitive user experience.

---

Please let me know if any further details are needed. Thank you for assisting with this feature request.

title: [BUG] Chatbox Application Resets Config.json Values on Launch
body:
**Bug Description:**
The Chatbox application automatically resets the values of specific parameters (`openaiMaxTokens`, `openaiMaxContextTokens`, and `openaiMaxContextMessageCount`) in the `config.json` file to their default values upon launch, even though different values were set in a previous session.

**Steps to Reproduce:**
To reproduce the bug:

1. Open the Chatbox application and set the following values:
   - `openaiMaxTokens`: 1024
   - `openaiMaxContextTokens`: 7168
   - `openaiMaxContextMessageCount`: 22
2. Close the Chatbox application.
3. Launch the Chatbox application by running `Chatbox.exe`.
4. Observe that the values of the parameters have been reset to their default values:
   - `openaiMaxTokens`: 0
   - `openaiMaxContextTokens`: 8000
   - `openaiMaxContextMessageCount`: 6

**Expected Results:**
The values of the parameters in the `config.json` file should persist across application sessions, and the application should not reset them to their default values upon launch.

**Actual Results:**
The values of the parameters in the `config.json` file are reset to their default values when the Chatbox application is launched, even though different values were set in a previous session.

**Desktop:**

-   Operating System: Windows 11
-   Application Version: 1.2.0

**Additional Context:**

- The "No Limit" option in the application for the `openaiMaxContextMessageCount` parameter sets the value to 22, which seems incorrect. This issue is separate from the main problem of the application resetting the parameter values but should also be addressed.

title: [Feature] Multiple openai API Hosts in settings
body:
**Problem Description**
I'm using ChatBox fox mistralai which offers an openai api, and I'm really liking it.
But I would also like to use openai and togetherai which both offers an openai api, and it's not possible without manually changing the settings between each requests to a different provider.

title: [Feature] CoPilot-level Model Parameter Arguments (Temperature, Top P, Max Tokens, etc)
body:
## **Problem Description**
System message for OpenAI is currently applied at the CoPilot level, while model parameter arguments are global.  As a result, all CoPilots must use the same arguments (Temperature, Top P, Max Length, etc) at any given time.  This severely limits the degree to which CoPilots are able to serve their unique intended purposes.

For example, consider a user who has defined a "Technical CoPilot" which includes a system message calling for certainty and demonstrated reasoning, it might make sense for this CoPilot to be used with arguments such as Temperature=0.5 and Max Response Tokens = 2000.

This same user also has a "TLDR Summarizer CoPilot" with a system message requesting concise summaries of concepts.  The user would likely prefer this CoPilot to use arguments such as Temperature=0.8 and Max Response Tokens < 200.


## **Proposed Solution**
Model parameter arguments should be configurable in the "Edit" view of each CoPilot, and should be individually enabled / disabled. 

- What are currently the global settings model parameter arguments would now become simply the default arguments.  

- If a CoPilot has all model parameter arguments configured, then the CoPilot settings take priority over the default settings.

- If a CoPilot has some model parameter arguments configured, then those will take priority over the default settings, while any disabled CoPilot arguments will default to the user's configured default settings.

- If a CoPilot does not have any model parameter arguments configured, then all arguments will default to the global settings arguments. 

## **Additional Context**
I don't have any further context to share, I think the request makes sense as is.  I'm happy to clarify and/or brainstorm further in the comments.

title: [Feature] Additional parameters for llama.cpp backend
body:
**Problem Description**
I'm [llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggerganov/llama.cpp) container as the backend (custom model) with this UI.
llama.cpp has/allows more message parameters/settings which are not present in OpenAI but could be provided as additional parameters.

The following parameters would be helpful to customise the sampling in llama.cpp further:
- top_k (top k tokens to choose from)
- n_keep (keeps the n tokens in cache - this stabilises perplexity for long-running-chat see https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.17453)
- typical_p (weighted version of top_p)
- mirostat (sampling via cross-entropy target see: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2007.14966.pdf)
  - mirostat_tau
  - miro_stat_eta


Preferably we should be able to specify additional custom/arbitrary json parameters for the `custom_model` settings.

**Proposed Solution**
Allow additional json parameters for `custom_model`

or add additional parameter support in settings to allow better sampling through `llama.cpp` backend.

**Additional Context**
The available parameters for llama.cpp can be found on https://github.com/ggerganov/llama.cpp/blob/master/examples/server/README.md

body:
The OpenAI API provider allows you to specify the API host, which is great to access OpenAI compatible APIs. However, the default API host is incorrect which makes it incompatible with some of these OpenAI compatible APIs. The code is targeting the /v1 API which has the `/chat/completions` endpoint. title: [Feature] Integrate Claude3 Language Model Support in ChatBox
body:
**Problem Description**

The current version of ChatBox does not support the recently released Claude3 language model from Anthropic. This limitation makes it difficult to leverage the improved capabilities and performance of the new model, which could potentially enhance the user experience and the quality of responses generated by the application.

**Proposed Solution**

Implement support for the Claude3 language model within the ChatBox application. This would involve integrating the necessary APIs and libraries provided by Anthropic to enable seamless communication with the Claude3 model. Additionally, the user interface should be updated to allow users to select the Claude3 model as an option when initiating a conversation or switching between models.

**Additional Context**

1. **Use Case**: Many users of ChatBox are interested in exploring the latest advancements in language models, and the ability to utilize Claude3 would cater to this demand. Enabling support for Claude3 would position ChatBox as a cutting-edge application that stays up-to-date with the latest developments in the field.

2. **Performance Improvements**: According to Anthropic's documentation, Claude3 offers improved performance and accuracy compared to previous versions, including better handling of context, increased knowledge retention, and more natural conversation flow. Integrating Claude3 could potentially enhance the overall user experience within ChatBox.

3. **API Documentation**: Anthropic provides comprehensive documentation and resources for integrating their language models, including Claude3. Following their guidelines and best practices would ensure a smooth and efficient implementation process.

4. **Compatibility**: It is essential to ensure that the integration of Claude3 does not break or negatively impact the existing functionality of ChatBox. Thorough testing and validation should be conducted to maintain compatibility with other supported language models and features.

By addressing this feature request, ChatBox would remain a competitive and relevant application in the rapidly evolving field of conversational AI, providing users with access to the latest advancements and enabling a more engaging and productive conversational experience.

body:
**Problem Description**
Unable to access chat history on other devices

**Proposed Solution**
Settings to sync chat history between devices in a private, customizeable manner.

To allow users to choose how their chat history and chatbots are synced. There are several ways to sync files between devices such as using Syncthing, cloud storage like Google Drive or Dropbox.

The syncing system should allow Chatbox to read and write chat history into a file onto the system to a directory the user can choose which the user can setup syncing that directory using Syncing or Google Drive or Dropbox, etc.

The files should be encrypted using a password that the user can set to prevent other programs or malware from reading the files. The directories and file names should also be encrypted to not make it clear what the directory or file stores.

A directory can store a chatbot data such as chat history and chatbot details and settings.

The chatbots should also be included and synced between devices. This way if you create a new chatbox on one device, it will be synced and added to the rest of your devices.

**Additional Context**
If chat history is in markdown, using Joplin Cloud is an option.

title: ChatGPT gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 support
body:
I really think it's a problem that the models are hard-coded into the app. It means that ChatBox is kind of failing at a core task for many developers, which is testing new models in a proper interface. ChatBox is chronically on a delay of about a month, and with the speed that updated models are released, it means that Chatbox will be running on old models 20%-30% of the time.

It's really a pity.

Sure, there are some models that require new feature support, e.g. media support. But the vast majority of updates from Anthropic and OpenAI are just a different model name put into a JSON field, and everything else is the same.

Isn't it time to get a Custom option, and then a specific model can be requested? This also allows testing with the weaker (but cheaper) models, which is still totally relevant for many kinds of software.

It's a super bummer with this ritual of every few months having to look again for ChatBox alternatives and trying to balance the various features of the many clients. You could, in 5 minutes, make this problem go away with a Custom field. And since it's custom, it sets the expectation correctly that it might not work without an update.

title: [Feature] Prompt Flow Integration / Builder
body:
### Feature Request: Prompt Flow Integration / Builder

#### Introduction
First of all, a massive load of gratitude to everyone! Being prepared for where AI is leading, I would like to propose the most important feature for the future of AI and possibly Chatbox!

#### Description
Implement a feature to create and manage prompt flows, similar to tools like Make.com and n8n.io, allowing users to chain multiple prompts together, passing the output from one prompt as input to the next, enabling more complex and multi-step workflows.

#### Use Cases
- Break down large tasks into smaller, more manageable steps
- Automate repetitive or multi-step processes involving LLMs
- Enable conditional branching and looping between Co-Pilots based on LLM outputs

#### Proposed Implementation
1. **Visual Flow Builder**: Provide a user-friendly interface to visually construct prompt flows, drag-and-drop prompts, and connect them with transitions.
2. **Prompt Library**: Allow users to create, save, and reuse custom prompts as building blocks for flows.
3. **Flow Variables**: Support passing data between prompts using variables or a shared context.
4. **Conditional Logic**: Enable branching and looping based on LLM outputs or user-defined conditions.
5. **Output Handling**: Provide options to save or export the final output from a prompt flow.

#### Similar Tools/Inspiration
- [Make.com](https://www.make.com/) (formerly Integromat)
- [n8n.io](https://n8n.io/)
- [Zapier](https://zapier.com/)

#### Additional Considerations
- Shareable and collaborative prompt flows
- Save, import, export flows as e.g. JSON/YAML for portability and backup
- Version control and revision history for prompt flows

title: [Feature]
body:
![2024-05-19_19h44_22](https://github.com/Bin-Huang/chatbox/assets/133587103/9db2430a-3b74-4ec1-965b-5b3854f5eca2)
**Problem Description**

Our chatbox currently encounters frequent issues with Google Gemini's safety settings, leading to erroneous rejections of mild content. This hampers the user experience and disrupts communication. The API often throws safety errors for messages that have negligible harmful content, such as simple greetings, which should not be flagged under categories like "HARM_CATEGORY_SEXUALLY_EXPLICIT" or similar. This overzealous filtering makes the software difficult and frustrating to use, as it falsely treats harmless messages as inappropriate.

**Proposed Solution**

Implement Google's safety parameters more accurately to reduce erroneous rejections of benign content. Specifically, adjust the sensitivity of the safety ratings to ensure that mild and safe communications are not flagged incorrectly. This adjustment will create a more reliable and user-friendly chat experience by preventing unnecessary interruptions due to overly cautious safety settings.

**Additional Context**

For reference, please see the attached screenshot that demonstrates a typical error message. This error occurred despite the message content being completely innocuous ("Hello"). The error message details are:

```
API Error: {"candidates":[{"finishReason":"SAFETY","index":0,"safetyRatings":[{"category":"HARM_CATEGORY_SEXUALLY_EXPLICIT","probability":"HIGH"},{"category":"HARM_CATEGORY_HATE_SPEECH","probability":"NEGLIGIBLE"},{"category":"HARM_CATEGORY_HARASSMENT","probability":"NEGLIGIBLE"},{"category":"HARM_CATEGORY_DANGEROUS_CONTENT","probability":"NEGLIGIBLE"}]}],"usageMetadata":{"promptTokenCount":1670,"totalTokenCount":1670}}
```

---

**问题描述**

我们的聊天框当前经常遇到 Google Gemini 安全设置的问题，导致对轻微内容的错误拒绝。这破坏了用户体验并干扰了沟通。API 经常会为内容极少有害的消息抛出安全错误，比如简单的问候，而这些并不应该被归类为“色情内容”或类似分类。这种过度严格的过滤使得软件难以使用，令人沮丧，因为它错误地将无害的消息视为不恰当内容。

**解决思路**

更准确地实施 Google 的安全参数，以减少对良性内容的错误拒绝。具体来说，调整安全评级的敏感度，以确保轻微和安全的通信不会被错误标记。这种调整将通过防止由于过于谨慎的安全设置而导致的不必要中断，创建一个更可靠和友好的聊天体验。

**附加上下文**

请参阅附件截图，该截图显示了典型的错误消息。这种错误发生在消息内容完全无辜的情况下（“Hello”）。错误消息详细信息如下：

```
API Error: {"candidates":[{"finishReason":"SAFETY","index":0,"safetyRatings":[{"category":"HARM_CATEGORY_SEXUALLY_EXPLICIT","probability":"HIGH"},{"category":"HARM_CATEGORY_HATE_SPEECH","probability":"NEGLIGIBLE"},{"category":"HARM_CATEGORY_HARASSMENT","probability":"NEGLIGIBLE"},{"category":"HARM_CATEGORY_DANGEROUS_CONTENT","probability":"NEGLIGIBLE"}]}],"usageMetadata":{"promptTokenCount":1670,"totalTokenCount":1670}}
```

title: [BUG] Android 1.3.13 (1.3.14) 选择ollama无法获得模型列表
body:
经初步尝试，1.3.14似乎仍存在这个问题
---

非常感谢这个项目！桌面端和安卓端迄今为止的使用感受都十分不错，随时随地能够通过chatbox使用大模型十分方便！但是最近在安卓端尝试接入ollama时遇到了问题。

经初步判断，此问题与 #1318 #1382(最新回复) #1426 是类似的。

**Bug 描述**
Android 1.3.13 选择模型提供方时，若选择ollama，无法获得模型列表。

**重现步骤**
我的ollama部署在远端集群，使用作业系统部署。
安卓端使用ssh -L进行端口映射，浏览器访问127.0.0.1:11434显示Ollama is running
 
1. 在遇到 #1318 前，作业脚本的设置主要为：
```shell
export OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0:11434
./ollama serve
``` 
在这个情况遇到了与 #1318 一模一样的情况，即桌面端（windows版 1.3.12 & 1.3.13）能够正常使用ollama模型，并获得模型列表的情况下，安卓端（Google Play版1.3.12 & 直接下载的1.3.13版）都出现了**选择模型提供方时，若选择ollama，无法获得模型列表**的情况。

在此情况下，我尝试了[Ollama-app](https://github.com/JHubi1/ollama-app)与[ChattUI](https://github.com/Vali-98/ChatterUI)，经验证，均能通过Ollama的Host test，并读取到集群上已安装的Ollama模型。

2. 此时，我的安卓端在Chatbox客户端和[Lobechat](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat)的[网页端](https://chat-preview.lobehub.com/)均无法读取Ollama模型。

3. 阅读 #1318 后，注意到软件中的***详细教程***指向[如何将 Chatbox 连接到远程 Ollama 服务：逐步指南](https://chatboxai.app/zh/help-center/connect-chatbox-remote-ollama-service-guide)。注意到，事实上Lobechat与Chatbox提供的解决方法一致。经修改后，我的作业脚本的主要相关设置为：
```shell
export OLLAMA_ORIGINS=*
export OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0:11434
./ollama serve
``` 
此后重新提交作业并在安卓端进行端口映射。此后，安卓手机上，浏览器能够访问127.0.0.1:11434显示Ollama is running，ChatterUI、Ollama app、Lobechat均能获得Ollama的模型列表，但Chatbox仍然获取不到😟。

***Chatbox Windows端从头至尾工作正常***

**期望结果**
Chatbox安卓端能够正常获取到远程主机上Ollama的列表模型，并进行正常交互。

**实际结果**
Chatbox安卓端无法获取到Ollama的列表模型，无法使用。

body:
**问题描述**
chatbox是一个非常优秀的项目，在使用chatbox过程中，配置了几个搭档，这几个搭档都有其专属的技能与人物设定，我希望这几个搭档可以组建一个团队。一起解决一个复杂的问题。当前的操作是在多个搭档间复制回复再提问，以解决复杂的问题。
如一个团队里有业务、需求、开发、测试等多个搭档。在同一个群组里，可以有多个搭档在里面进行对话以解决问题。
望采纳，感谢

**解决思路**
1、创建群组，群组里添加配置好的搭档。可以随时添加和删除搭档（可以参考钉钉的群设置界面，参见下方的附加）
2、对话过程中，使用@搭档的方式或在某段对话下@搭档引用，让这一搭档进行回复，这回复这过程中，该搭档结合自身的设定、用户新输入的内容和引用的对话进行回复
3、各个搭档可以配置不同的模型接口，如业务人设用openAI，需求人设用Ollama，开发人设用Claude等
4、为了避免token过度使用，可以设定只有@的搭档时调用API，其他搭档没有被@不调用API，调用API时传的上下文内容只传该搭档的回复过的内容及被@的内容

I would like a reliable way to access the latest chat records on all devices, ensuring data integrity and consistency. **Proposed Solution** I would like to see an automated chat history backup and synchronization feature based on the WebDav protocol. Specifically, whenever a user engages in a chat on any device, Chatbox should automatically back up the chat history to a user-specified WebDav server. This will not only synchronize records across all devices but also provide users with additional data security. Add a configuration option in the application settings to allow users to enter server address, username, and password for the WebDav server. Provide options for automatic and manual backups, allowing users to choose between automatic backup after each chat or periodic manual backups. Ensure data security during the backup and synchronization process by using encrypted transmission protocols, such as HTTPS, to protect user privacy. Automatically synchronize the latest chat history from the WebDav server when logging in on different devices. **问题描述** Chatbox是一款优秀的跨平台产品，我在多个个人电脑和手机上均使用了这个产品。然而，当前的版本缺乏一个自动化的聊天记录备份和同步机制，这使得在不同设备间切换时，聊天记录无法保持一致。我希望能够通过一个可靠的方式，在所有设备上获取最新的聊天记录，以确保信息的完整性和一致性。 **解决思路** 我希望看到一种基于WebDav协议的自动聊天记录备份和同步功能。具体来说，当用户在任何设备上进行聊天时，Chatbox能够自动将聊天记录备份到用户指定的WebDav服务器中。这不仅可以在所有设备上同步记录，还能为用户提供额外的数据安全保障。 在应用设置中添加WebDav服务器配置选项，允许用户输入服务器地址、用户名和密码等信息。 提供自动和手动备份选项，用户可以选择在每次聊天后自动备份，或者定期手动备份。 确保备份和同步过程中的数据安全性，使用加密传输协议（如HTTPS）保护用户隐私。 在不同设备上登录时，自动从WebDav服务器同步最新的聊天记录。 **附加上下文** 一个典型的用例是用户在家中的电脑上使用Chatbox与AI聊天后，在外出时希望继续在手机上进行对话，而无需手动导入或同步记录。 提供一个设置页面的截图，展示如何配置WebDav服务器信息，以及用户可以选择的备份和同步选项。

title: [BUG] Other Software's File Monitoring Leads to High CPU Usage While Generating Messages
body:
I have noticed that after each Chatbox query, my Windows Antimalware Service Executable process goes crazy - enough for my older machine to stutter for a little while (20-30 seconds) until it finishes doing what it's doing.

1. Go to Chatbox.
2. Query the AI - I am using OpenAI 4o-mini.
3. In Task Manager observe the "Antimalware Service Executable - Microsoft Defender Antivirus Service" process immediately start using 100% of a core.

**Expected Results**
I wouldn't expect the antimalware process to be triggered to this extent, upon each AI query.

**Actual Results**
System slow down due to above.

**Desktop (please complete the following information):**

- Operating System: Windows 10 fully updated
- Application Version: Chatbox 1.5.1
- Model: OpenAI chatgpt-4o-mini

**Testing**
Using Process Monitor I can see the issue may be Chatbox continually calling CreateFile on filenames like these.
C:\Users\<username>\AppData\Roaming\xyz.chatboxapp.app\config.json.tmp-0421289212bd01f0
C:\Users\<username>\AppData\Roaming\xyz.chatboxapp.app\config.json.tmp-0421289885032997
C:\Users\<username>\AppData\Roaming\xyz.chatboxapp.app\config.json.tmp-0421290572318334
C:\Users\<username>\AppData\Roaming\xyz.chatboxapp.app\config.json.tmp-04212912532c1376
C:\Users\<username>\AppData\Roaming\xyz.chatboxapp.app\config.json.tmp-04212989060e02da

This continues on for 20-30 seconds - well after the AI response has completed, ie. all the while antimalware is triggered, checking these files I assume.

**Workaround**
I added a Windows Security exclusion on the xyz.chatboxapp.app folder - obviously not ideal.

title: [Feature] Add integrations to allow chatting with external services i.e Google Calendar, Bing etc.
body:
**Problem Description**
Add support to use Chatbox interface as convenient UI for other services which could be queried via API using natural language, such as but not limited to: Google Calendar, or web search, or Jira, or any other.

Langchain supports such integrations with various platforms which allow to use natural language as a way to communicate with external services. [Here is a full list](https://python.langchain.com/docs/integrations/tools/).

This feature could also mirror what's already available in one commercial application I found, [Alice App](https://www.heyalice.app/). I assume it works very similar to how Langchain does that: extract intent from text (i.e get my schedule for today) -> query GCalendar using integration -> analyse return data, probably in programmatic form (JSON) -> represent it to user in human-like description.

**Proposed Solution**
Few ideas on how could it look:
- a new plugins functionality which would allow users to create their integrations, maybe even entire flows
- a hardcoded set of chats, each with support for very specific purpose ie. one for Calendar, one for Jira, etc, just like currently there are some chats provided out of the box i.e image generation.
- perhaps, support for setting an action in text field with use of some command syntax, which could be called in all chats. Something like: `@jira list my current sprint` or `@gcal add new appointment at 2am`. That would set wanted action explicitly by user, without leaving the decision what to do to LLM.
